title: A secreted endosymbiont protein essential for colonizing host cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the only Figshare file, SyeA_Datasets.xlsx (242 KB, CC BY 4.0), and read all 9 sheets. S1 has 572 raw rows (about 569 proteins after the 3 header rows), holding BastionX (a type-3 secretion effector predictor) scores and yes/no calls for the Buchnera APS proteome. S2 to S6 are about 105 to 116 rows each, covering genome lists and presence/absence of syeA and flagellar genes across Buchnera genomes. S7 has 92 rows of AlphaFold3 interaction scores. S8 has 27 rows of digital PCR (dPCR) knockdown checks. S9 has 308 rows of lysosome-staining measurements from microscope images.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The contents of the PRIDE proteomics deposit PXD066113. I did not open it; the paper describes mass-spectrometry proteomics for one study. The Europe PMC supplement listing timed out, so I could not inspect the Nature 'Source data' files.

a1_downloadable.note: The Figshare xlsx downloaded with no login (CC BY 4.0). PRIDE PXD066113 is public according to the paper, but I did not open it.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only per-protein labels are the yes/no calls in S1 (whether a protein is predicted to be a type-3 secreted effector) and gene presence/absence in S4 to S6. No column holds a measured biological outcome that a model could learn.

a3_inputs_present.note: S1 lists RefSeq protein accessions (WP_...) with no sequences, so every sequence would have to be fetched from NCBI. That is feasible for about 569 proteins, but the inputs are not in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: The scores are unitless BastionX probabilities, and S9 uses image intensities in arbitrary units. Units are not a problem here.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest sheet (S1) has about 569 proteins from one genome, and every other sheet has 30 to 308 rows. That is below the roughly 1,500-row threshold, and the S1 labels are not measured anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 103 syeA orthologues in S5 and the 113 to 115 genomes in S4 and S6 match the counts in the paper text.

a8_label_provenance.note: The S1 effector labels are BastionX predictions and the S7 interaction scores are AlphaFold3 predictions, so both labels are model outputs. Training on them would only copy those models.

existing_models.name: BastionX (type-3 secretion effector predictor, used in the paper itself)
existing_models.score_and_split: The paper cites an earlier version, Bastion3, at a 4.1% false-positive rate. I did not retrieve BastionX's own benchmark.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would fit protein sequences, but there are no measured labels to train on.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None found: the per-protein labels are predictions, and the measured data is a single-gene knockdown experiment.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here would only reproduce BastionX's effector calls for one roughly 569-protein endosymbiont proteome. It would learn nothing measured.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use bacterial protein sequences to predict which proteins are secreted into host cells.
plain_idea.train_on: About 569 proteins from the aphid endosymbiont Buchnera (strain APS), given only as accession numbers with no sequences.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each protein is a type-3 secreted effector, a protein the bacterium injects into host cells. The 'true' answers here are another program's (BastionX's) predictions, not lab measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Finding secreted effectors in endosymbionts that cannot be grown in the lab would guide knockdown experiments. This data cannot support that, because it has no measured labels and too few rows.

ml_idea: Not viable. The only per-protein table is the output of an existing secretion predictor (BastionX). The measured data (dPCR knockdown checks and lysosome-staining images, under 310 rows) comes from one gene in one aphid species.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project fails Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done: opened the xlsx. The largest sheet has about 569 rows, and its labels are BastionX predictions.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A5 and A8. The Figshare workbook (9 sheets, at most about 569 rows) holds only model predictions (BastionX effector calls, AlphaFold3 interaction scores), presence/absence tables for about 113 genomes, and small single-gene knockdown measurements. Nothing measured is large enough to learn from.
